subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The 'golden triangle' in sport refers to the relationship between:
questions.explain: The golden triangle describes the interdependent link between sport, the media and sponsorship/commercialisation.

questions.q: Commercialisation in sport is the process of:
options: Treating sport as a product to make a profit
questions.explain: Commercialisation involves managing sport as a business to generate income, linked closely to the media and sponsorship.

questions.q: Which strategy is commonly used to reduce football hooliganism?
options: Encouraging standing terraces with no segregation
questions.explain: All-seater stadia, CCTV, segregation of fans and alcohol controls help reduce spectator violence.

questions.q: Hawk-Eye technology is mainly used in sport to:
options: Aid officials in making accurate decisions
questions.explain: Hawk-Eye helps officials make accurate decisions on close calls, improving fairness.

questions.q: A benefit of sponsorship for a performer is that it:
options: Provides funding for equipment, coaching and travel
questions.explain: Sponsorship provides financial support that helps athletes afford training, coaching and competition.

questions.q: How can age affect participation in sport?
options: It has no effect on participation
Only the cost of membership matters
Some activities suit certain ages and older people may have less mobility
questions.explain: Age can affect participation through changing physical ability, suitability of activities and available time.

questions.q: How can technology such as wearable heart-rate monitors benefit training?
options: By replacing the need for a coach completely
By providing accurate data to monitor and adjust intensity
questions.explain: Wearable technology gives accurate, objective data that helps performers train at the correct intensity.

questions.q: Why might an athlete take a stimulant such as a banned amphetamine?
options: To increase alertness and reduce tiredness
questions.explain: Stimulants increase alertness and mask fatigue, but they are banned and carry serious health risks.

questions.q: Which is an example of gamesmanship?
options: Time-wasting to gain an advantage within the rules
questions.explain: Gamesmanship is stretching the rules to gain an advantage without actually breaking them.

questions.q: A negative consequence of taking performance-enhancing drugs is:
options: Serious health risks and bans from sport
questions.explain: PEDs damage health and, if detected, lead to bans, loss of sponsorship and a damaged reputation.

questions.q: Which is a benefit of commercialisation for spectators?
options: Less choice of sport to watch
Greater access to sport through television and online streaming
questions.explain: Commercialisation increases media coverage, giving spectators more access to watch a wide range of sport.

questions.q: Sportsmanship is best shown by:
options: Deliberately fouling to stop a goal
questions.explain: Sportsmanship involves fair play, honesty and respect for opponents and officials.

questions.q: Which is a drawback of sponsorship for a performer?
options: Pressure to perform and behave well to keep the sponsor
questions.explain: Sponsorship can bring pressure to perform and maintain a positive image, with funding lost if standards drop.

questions.q: Wheelchair-accessible facilities are important for increasing participation among people with:
questions.explain: Suitable provision and access help remove barriers to participation for people with disabilities.

questions.q: Goal-line technology in football is an example of technology used to:
options: Give officials accurate decisions on whether the ball crossed the line
questions.explain: Goal-line technology helps officials decide accurately whether the whole ball has crossed the goal line.

questions.q: Hooliganism among spectators is an example of:
questions.explain: Hooliganism is violent or disorderly spectator behaviour, a form of deviance associated with sport.

questions.q: Why might a performer take performance-enhancing drugs such as anabolic steroids?
options: To slow their heart rate for relaxation
To increase muscle growth and train harder
questions.explain: Anabolic steroids are taken to increase muscle mass and allow harder training, but they are banned and harmful.

questions.q: A negative effect of the media's influence on sport is:
options: Loss of atmosphere when fewer fans attend live events
questions.explain: Demand for televised sport can reduce live attendance and focus coverage on a few popular sports.

questions.q: A reason why some women have historically participated less in sport is:
options: There are no women's competitions at all
They are physically unable to play sport
questions.explain: Barriers such as stereotyping, fewer role models and less media coverage have lowered female participation.

questions.q: Which of these is a socio-economic factor affecting participation in sport?
options: The cost of equipment and membership
questions.explain: Socio-economic factors include cost, income and the affordability of equipment and facilities.

questions.q: Deviance in sport refers to:
options: Behaviour that goes against the accepted norms and rules
questions.explain: Deviance is behaviour such as cheating, doping or violence that breaks the moral or written rules of sport.

questions.q: A disadvantage of the media's demand to schedule matches at certain times is that it can:
options: Be inconvenient for live spectators and disrupt players' routines
questions.explain: Media scheduling can move events to awkward times, inconveniencing fans and players to suit broadcasters.
